28Oct 2026Sensitive Light: Geometry, Chaos, and Information Recovery in Null Transport

How sensitively does light propagation depend on initial conditions, and how much source information survives partial observation? The ratio of Lyapunov exponent to orbital frequency organizes predictability across black holes, a wormhole throat and plasma lenses; the one genuinely chaotic system computed, the Majumdar–Papapetrou di-hole, confines its chaos to a thin fractal set whose outcomes remain 99.3% recoverable under coarse-graining.

Five ways out of debt: Britain's century-long grind, America's postwar financial repression, Sweden's legislated rules, Canada's cuts, Belgium's euro-anchored surpluses. The repression did more work than the surpluses. Japan and Italy are the red flags.

Five disinflations, one anatomy: deeply positive real yields, a named credible policymaker, and a forcing crisis preceded every bond rally. Israel killed 445% inflation with GDP growing; Turkey's real rates sat above 30% for two years into reform.

20Oct 2026Frontier Sovereign Bond Returns in Dollar Terms: Carry, Currency, and Default Risk

In dollar terms the frontier carry trade does not survive: Ghana earned -78% and Kyrgyzstan -13% from 2010 to 2024. Starting yield still predicts forward dollar returns at long horizons, but the currency eats half the local carry; rising debt-to-GDP, not IMF programs, is the ruin signal.

18Oct 2026Small Seeds, Thin Markets: Climate Risk, Supply Chains, and the Economics of Sesame from Farm to Fast Food

A 50% price spike costs the average McDonald's $98 a year, but allergen law and rigid supplier approvals turn a short shortage into an operational crisis.
